Literature Overview

TitlePhotothermal oxidative dehydrogenation of propane to propylene over Cu/BN catalysts
DOI10.3389/fchem.2024.1439185
Typeresearch_article
Catalyst SystemCu/BN catalysts with unique morphologies, specifically Cu/BN-NS and Cu/BN-NF, for a photothermal ODHP system
Reaction TypePhotothermal oxidative dehydrogenation of propane (ODHP) to propylene
ClassificationReaction: oxidative_dehydrogenation, photothermal_catalysis | Catalyst: metal_nanoparticle
Key ClaimCu/BN-NS and Cu/BN-NF with enlarged specific surface areas exhibited higher catalytic activities, and the LSPR effect of Cu nanoparticles enhanced photothermal ODHP performance under visible light irradiation; this is reported as the first BN-based photothermal ODHP catalytic system.
Statistics0 objects, 0 relationships

Catalyst Design

FieldValueStatus / Origin
catalyst_system Cu/BN catalysts with unique morphologies (Cu/BN-NS, Cu/BN-NF, Cu/BN-NP) with 1.0 wt% Cu loading on BN supports REPORTED ORIGINAL_EXPERIMENT
catalyst_type supported metal nanoparticle catalyst REPORTED ORIGINAL_EXPERIMENT
active_component Cu nanoparticles, 1.0 wt% REPORTED ORIGINAL_EXPERIMENT
support boron nitride (BN) with different morphologies: nanosheets (BN-NS), nanofibers (BN-NF), and nanoparticles (BN-NP) REPORTED ORIGINAL_EXPERIMENT
synthesis_method wetness impregnation REPORTED ORIGINAL_EXPERIMENT
synthesis_conditions stirring at room temperature at 500 r/min for 10 h, dried at 100°C in air, reduced in 10% H2/N2 mixture at 500°C for 3 h REPORTED ORIGINAL_EXPERIMENT
reaction_type photothermal oxidative dehydrogenation of propane (ODHP) to propylene REPORTED ORIGINAL_EXPERIMENT
design_rationale To overcome the challenge of achieving high activity and high propylene selectivity simultaneously in ODHP by utilizing the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effect of Cu nanoparticles to enhance photothermal catalytic performance under visible light irradiation REPORTED ORIGINAL_EXPERIMENT

Figure 2

FIGURE 2 (A) Adsorption-desorption isotherms and (B) pore size distributions of BN supports and Cu/BN catalysts.
VLM Scientific Observations (12 records)
Panel A is a line graph showing adsorption isotherms for six different materials, with adsorbed volume (V_a) on the y-axis and relative pressure (P/P₀) on the x-axis.
IMAGE_ONLY_OBSERVATION CANDIDATE Confidence: HIGH
Panel B is a line graph showing pore size distributions (dV_p/dr_p) for the same six materials, with pore size on the x-axis and differential pore volume on the y-axis.
IMAGE_ONLY_OBSERVATION CANDIDATE Confidence: HIGH
The adsorption-desorption isotherms for all BN supports and Cu/BN catalysts show a Type II behavior with a hysteresis loop at high relative pressure (P/P₀ > 0.8), indicating the presence of mesopores.
IMAGE_ONLY_OBSERVATION CANDIDATE Confidence: HIGH
BN-NS exhibits the highest adsorption volume (Vₐ) among all samples, followed by BN-NF and BN-NP, suggesting a higher surface area for BN-NS.
IMAGE_ONLY_OBSERVATION CANDIDATE Confidence: HIGH
The Cu/BN catalysts (Cu/BN-NS, Cu/BN-NF, Cu/BN-NP) show lower adsorption volumes compared to their corresponding BN supports (BN-NS, BN-NF, BN-NP), indicating a reduction in surface area or pore volume upon Cu loading.
IMAGE_ONLY_OBSERVATION CANDIDATE Confidence: HIGH
BN-NS has a broad pore size distribution centered around 10–100 nm, while BN-NF and BN-NP show narrower distributions with peaks at smaller pore sizes (<10 nm).
IMAGE_ONLY_OBSERVATION CANDIDATE Confidence: HIGH
The pore size distributions of Cu/BN catalysts are shifted to smaller pore sizes compared to their corresponding BN supports, indicating pore blockage or narrowing due to Cu deposition.
TEXT_SUPPORTED_STATEMENT CANDIDATE Confidence: HIGH
The Cu/BN-NP sample exhibits the smallest pore size distribution peak, suggesting the most significant pore blockage among the catalysts.
IMAGE_ONLY_OBSERVATION CANDIDATE Confidence: HIGH
The BN-NS support has the largest pore volume, as indicated by the highest dVₚ/drₚ value in the pore size distribution plot.
IMAGE_ONLY_OBSERVATION CANDIDATE Confidence: HIGH
The pore size distribution of BN-NF is bimodal, with peaks at approximately 2–5 nm and 10–20 nm.
MODEL_INFERENCE CANDIDATE Confidence: MEDIUM
The hysteresis loop in the isotherms is consistent with capillary condensation in mesopores, which is typical for materials with pore sizes between 2 and 50 nm.
MODEL_INFERENCE CANDIDATE Confidence: MEDIUM
The Cu/BN-NF catalyst shows a pore size distribution peak at a smaller pore size than BN-NF, suggesting that Cu nanoparticles are deposited within the pores, reducing their effective diameter.
TEXT_SUPPORTED_STATEMENT CANDIDATE Confidence: HIGH

Evidence (30)

Cu/BN-NS and Cu/BN-NF have enlarged specific surface areas and exhibit higher catalytic activities.
The LSPR effect of Cu nanoparticles enhances the photothermal catalytic performance of Cu/BN catalysts under visible light irradiation.
A BN-based photothermal ODHP catalytic system was established for the first time.
BN offers high propylene selectivity in ODHP but is limited by insufficient light absorption, rapid electron-hole pair recombination, and high-temperature water-vapor-induced deactivation.
Cu/BN-NS and Cu/BN-NF were designed with unique morphologies and enlarged specific surface areas; these features are associated with higher catalytic activities.
The localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effect of Cu nanoparticles enhances photothermal catalytic performance under visible light irradiation.
